modelIntro.title: What Is Wan 2.6 AI Video Generator?
description: Wan 2.6 is the Wan version for turning a promising idea into a longer review cut. It keeps the setup simple—text or one reference image—while giving you up to 15 seconds to show a readable sequence.

Choose it after the concept is already worth developing: product walkthroughs, recipe or assembly steps, retail displays, beauty motions, training clips, and sound-timed drafts that need a beginning, action detail, and final hold.

faq.q: What makes Wan 2.6 a review-cut model?
faq.a: Wan 2.6 gives a validated idea enough room to show setup, action detail, audio timing, and a final hold. It is stronger after the cheap screening step, not before it.

faq.q: When should I choose the 15-second option?
faq.a: Choose 15 seconds when reviewers need to inspect more than a hook: a product walkthrough, an assembly step, a retail display move, or a recipe beat with beginning, middle, and hold.

faq.q: How should I structure a Wan 2.6 prompt?
faq.a: Write it like a compact timeline: setup, main action, detail moment, stable elements, audio cue, and final hold. This helps reviewers judge pacing and continuity.

faq.q: Does Wan 2.6 work from one reference image?
faq.a: Yes. Use one uploaded image when packaging, room layout, product shape, face, or object identity should stay recognizable across the longer clip.

faq.q: What audio details should I include?
faq.a: Name practical audio moments such as tool clicks, packaging contact, fabric movement, ingredient handling, room ambience, surface scrape, or final quiet hold.

faq.q: Is Wan 2.6 the right choice for client approval?
faq.a: Yes, when the client needs to understand timing and motion before final production. It gives more context than Wan 2.5 while keeping the setup simple.
Avoid it when you are still testing many cheap hooks; use Wan 2.5 first. Also avoid it when the project still lacks a clear sequence, stable reference, or audio plan.

faq.q: How many Toolaze Credits does Wan 2.6 cost?
faq.a: Wan 2.6 starts at 140 Credits for 720p 5-second output. Longer duration or 1080p output increases the required Credits before generation.

faq.q: Does Wan 2.6 need a separate ending image?
faq.a: No. Wan 2.6 is built around text or one reference image, a compact timeline, native audio cues, and a final hold generated from the prompt.

promptExamples.title: Wan 2.6 Review-Cut Prompts
promptExamples.subtitle: Use these when a concept has moved past cheap screening and needs timing, audio, and a clearer review sequence.

items.title: 15-Second Product Walkthrough
items.prompt: Create a 15-second review draft from the uploaded product image. Open on the full package, move into a close detail of the texture and label, show a hand interaction, then end with a stable final hold. Add soft studio ambience, packaging contact sounds, and a clean product placement rhythm.
items.description: Uses Wan 2.6 for a fuller product review sequence.

items.title: Training Step Draft
items.prompt: Generate a clear instructional clip showing a technician placing a small part, tightening one screw, checking alignment, and pausing for the final inspection. Keep the camera steady, the hands readable, and each step separated by natural tool sounds so reviewers can follow the action.
items.description: Shows why Wan 2.6 fits readable instructional motion.

items.title: Retail Display Motion
items.prompt: Animate the uploaded storefront display as a 10-second brand review cut. Start with a wide view, push slowly toward the featured shelf, let small lights turn on in sequence, and finish on the hero product. Keep signage, packaging edges, and shelf layout stable while adding gentle store ambience.
items.description: Uses one image as an anchor for a longer display draft.

items.title: Sound-Led Recipe Beat
items.prompt: Create a 15-second overhead cooking draft: ingredients slide into place, sauce pours into a bowl, a spoon stirs twice, and the final plated texture holds for review. Add pour, scrape, bowl contact, and soft kitchen room tone. Keep the sequence paced for stakeholder feedback.

troubleshooting.title: Prompt Tips for Wan 2.6 Review Cuts
troubleshooting.subtitle: Wan 2.6 works best when the prompt reads like a compact timeline for reviewers.

items.title: Write timeline beats
items.desc: Weak prompt: make it professional. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Build a 15-second review timeline: three seconds of setup, six seconds of the main handling action, three seconds for detail texture, then a final three-second hold for feedback. Keep camera speed slow and stable.

items.title: Name what reviewers must inspect
items.desc: Weak prompt: show the product nicely. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Show the closure, seam, label edge, and hand contact clearly enough for stakeholder review. Keep the package shape consistent, add soft studio ambience, and pause on the final front-facing view.

items.title: Pair pacing with audio
items.desc: Weak prompt: add sound. Better prompt:
items.prompt: Time the audio to the review sequence: room tone during setup, one soft tool click during the action, a light surface scrape during the detail moment, and a quiet final ambience bed during the hold.
